reviewerFinding.title: Missing focused tests for environment parsing and propagation
reviewerFinding.effect: The initial Luna implementation satisfied the runtime contract but largely omitted the focused regression coverage explicitly requested. Terra review identified the missing coverage; the same Luna implementer added parser/default/propagation/reporting/secret-non-disclosure tests; Terra delta review then returned CLEAN.

runs.finding: Coordinator planned the feature, Terra Worker A implemented it with focused tests in one pass, GPT-5.4 mini Worker B independently converged, and Terra strong review returned CLEAN.

interpretation: The leading economical topology survives the first larger stage-two cross-cutting feature and passes the independent compatibility/security oracle.

This run is important because the strong reviewer found a real omission in the cheap implementation: requested regression coverage was missing. Same-implementer remediation closed the gap without introducing a coordinator or Worker B.

The economical path used slightly more model calls and input tokens than v0.2 because it required a second implementation/review cycle, but it still used about 54% fewer AI credits and 17% less wall time.

The result strengthens the argument that independent strong review is the core assurance mechanism while the persistent coordinator/peer can remain conditional; it also shows that raw call/token count is not the only efficiency metric when model tier differs substantially.
